This implies that (2S)-3',4'-Dihydroxy-6,7-Dimethoxyflavan may act through a pathway where it modulates the activity of these intermediates, ultimately influencing ATR function. The evidence suggests a possible mechanism involving the activation or inhibition of translation initiation factors, which could then affect ATR activity.
